title: Personal Pronouns and PNG Suffixes
subtitle: Match subject pronouns with Person-Number-Gender verb endings
keyPoint: Tamil finite verbs must agree with their subject pronoun using mandatory Person-Number-Gender (PNG) terminal suffixes.

mistakes.note: The pronoun நான் (1st person singular) requires the ending -ஏன், not the 3rd person masculine -ஆன்.
Feminine singular அவள் must agree with the feminine suffix -ஆள், not the masculine -ஆன்.
Plural subject நாங்கள் requires the plural suffix -ஓம் instead of the singular -ஏன்.

quiz.question: Select the correct verb to complete: 'நான் பாடம் ___.' (I study a lesson.)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular pronoun நான் requires the PNG suffix -ஏன் (படிக்கிறேன்).

quiz.question: Select the correct verb to complete: 'அவன் சென்னைக்கு ___.' (He goes to Chennai.)
quiz.explanation: The masculine pronoun அவன் requires the masculine suffix -ஆன் (போகிறான்).

quiz.question: Select the correct verb to complete: 'நீ என்ன ___?' (What are you doing?)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person pronoun நீ pairs with the suffix -ஆய் (செய்கிறாய்).

quiz.question: Select the correct verb to complete: 'அவள் வேகமாக ___.' (She runs fast.)
quiz.explanation: The feminine pronoun அவள் takes the suffix -ஆள் (ஓடுகிறாள்).

tip: Because PNG suffixes explicitly indicate person, number, and gender, subject pronouns like நான் or அவள் are frequently dropped in everyday speech.

title: Equational Sentences (Zero Copula)
subtitle: Link two noun phrases without an overt verb 'to be'
keyPoint: Present-tense identity and classification sentences in Tamil place the subject and predicate noun directly side by side with no copula verb.

mistakes.note: Do not insert the existential verb இருக்கிறார் to mean 'is' when stating identity or profession.
இருக்கிறது indicates location or existence, not equational definition.
Simply place the subject and the predicate noun adjacent to one another.

quiz.question: How do you say 'This is my house' in Tamil?
quiz.explanation: Equational identity sentences omit the verb 'to be' in the present tense: இது என் வீடு.

quiz.question: Complete the equational sentence: 'ராமு ஒரு ___.' (Ramu is a student.)
quiz.explanation: A predicate noun (மாணவன்) is placed directly after the subject with no connecting copula verb.

quiz.question: Which of the following correctly means 'He is a doctor'?
quiz.explanation: In standard present equational sentences, no verb is used: அவர் மருத்துவர்.

quiz.question: What is the function of zero copula in 'அது நல்ல புத்தகம்'?
options: To express nominal identity without a verb
To express location of the book
quiz.explanation: Juxtaposing 'அது' and 'நல்ல புத்தகம்' forms an equational sentence meaning 'That is a good book'.

tip: Save the verb இரு (இருக்கிறேன், இருக்கிறது) exclusively for location ('I am in Chennai') or existence ('There is water'), never for equivalence.

title: Dative Case (-ukku) and Experiencer Subjects
subtitle: Express indirect objects, feelings, desires, and necessity
keyPoint: Add -க்கு / -உக்கு (-kku / -ukku) to mark recipients, destinations, and subjects experiencing internal sensations or needs.

cells: To him is hungry (He is hungry)

mistakes.note: Experiencer predicates like பிடிக்கும் require the subject in the dative case (எனக்கு), not the nominative (நான்).
Involuntary sensations like hunger take a dative subject (அவனுக்கு).
Desire or need with வேண்டும் must be paired with the dative marker -உக்கு.

quiz.question: Choose the right pronoun: '___ தமிழ் தெரியும்.' (I know Tamil.)
quiz.explanation: The stative verb தெரியும் (to know) governs a dative experiencer subject (எனக்கு).

quiz.question: Choose the right form: 'அவன் ___ போகிறான்.' (He goes to the shop.)
quiz.explanation: The destination of motion requires the dative case marker -க்கு (கடைக்கு).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'அவருக்குக் காப்பி ___.' (He wants coffee.)
quiz.explanation: வேண்டும் (want/need) is an impersonal verb paired with the dative experiencer அவருக்கு.

quiz.question: Select the correct subject: '___ பசிக்கிறது.' (The child is hungry.)
quiz.explanation: Physical sensations take the experiencer in the dative case: குழந்தைக்கு.

tip: Think of dative experiencers as 'To me it is likable' (எனக்கு பிடிக்கும்) or 'To him it is needed' (அவனுக்கு வேண்டும்) instead of English 'I like' or 'He wants'.

title: Accusative Case (-ai) and Object Marking
subtitle: Mark definite or animate direct objects with -ஐ
keyPoint: The accusative suffix -ஐ (-ai) is mandatory for animate direct objects and definite inanimate objects, but omitted for generic inanimate nouns.

mistakes.note: Animate human objects must always carry the accusative suffix -ஐ (மருத்துவரை).
Animate non-human objects such as animals require -ஐ when they are specific targets of an action.
Generic inanimate everyday food or drink objects typically drop the accusative suffix.

quiz.question: Select the correct form: 'நான் ___ கூப்பிட்டேன்.' (I called Kumar.)
quiz.explanation: Human direct objects must take the accusative suffix -ஐ (குமாரை).

quiz.question: Which sentence naturally omits the accusative suffix for a generic object?
quiz.explanation: Drinking water in general does not require -ஐ; plain 'தண்ணீர் குடித்தான்' is natural Differential Object Marking.

quiz.question: Select the correct object: 'அந்த ___ எடு.' (Take that book.)
quiz.explanation: Definite specific inanimate nouns (indicated by அந்த) take the accusative marker (புத்தகத்தை).

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'அம்மா ___ தூக்கினார்.' (Mother lifted the baby.)
quiz.explanation: The human object குழந்தை must take the accusative marker -ஐ, becoming குழந்தையை.

tip: Ask yourself: Is the object human or specific? If yes, attach -ஐ. If it is an indefinite, non-living mass noun like tea or rice, leave it unmarked.

title: Existential vs Categorical Negation (illai vs alla)
subtitle: Distinguish non-existence/absence from non-identity
keyPoint: Use இல்லை (illai) to negate presence, possession, or verbal actions, and அல்ல (alla) to deny category or identity.

cells: Something does not exist/is not there

mistakes.note: To say milk is not present in the house, use existential இல்லை, never identity-negating அல்ல.
Negating verb actions in the past uses the infinitive + இல்லை, not அல்ல.
Absence of people ('nobody is there') demands இல்லை.

quiz.question: Complete the existential negation: 'பையில் பணம் ___.' (There is no money in the bag.)
quiz.explanation: The absence or non-existence of an item in a location is negated with இல்லை.

quiz.question: Complete the identity negation: 'அவர் மருத்துவர் ___.' (He is not a doctor.)
quiz.explanation: Denying a nominal category or role ('X is not Y') in formal Tamil uses அல்ல.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I did not eat' using the verb infinitive சாப்பிட?
quiz.explanation: Verbal past negation is formed with infinitive + இல்லை (சாப்பிடவில்லை / சாப்பிட இல்லை).

quiz.question: What is the primary difference between இல்லை and அல்ல?
options: இல்லை is future, அல்ல is past
இல்லை negates existence/actions, அல்ல negates noun identity
இல்லை is only for plurals, அல்ல for singulars
இல்லை is for questions, அல்ல is for answers
quiz.explanation: இல்லை marks non-existence, absence, or non-action, whereas அல்ல specifically asserts that a noun is not another noun.

tip: Simple rule of thumb: If you can replace the sentence with 'There is no...', use இல்லை. If you can rephrase as 'X is not the same as Y', use அல்ல.

title: Interrogative Particles (-aa, -ee, -oo)
subtitle: Forming questions and expressing doubt with clitics
keyPoint: Attach the clitic vowel -aa to any word in a sentence to transform it into a polar yes/no question targeting that specific constituent.

mistakes.note: Do not attach the yes/no question particle -aa when an interrogative pronoun like 'what' (என்ன) is already present.
The particle -aa is a bound clitic and must attach directly to the verb through sandhi rules, not written as an independent word.
Place -aa on the verb for neutral inquiry; attaching it to the subject emphasizes 'Was it SHE who came?'.

quiz.question: Choose the question: 'Did you read the book?'
quiz.explanation: The suffix -aa attached to the finite verb வாசித்தாய் produces the question வாசித்தாயா.

quiz.question: Identify the word expressing doubt or hesitation: 'Will he come?'
quiz.explanation: The suffix -oo expresses doubt, uncertainty, or wonder.

quiz.question: Select the sentence meaning 'Is this tea?'
quiz.explanation: Adding -aa to தேநீர் (tea) yields the direct yes/no interrogative தேநீரா.

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'Only today did I see him'?
quiz.explanation: The clitic -ee attached to இன்று (today) forms the emphatic இன்றே (only today/this very day).

tip: Whichever word gets the -aa suffix becomes the exact focus of your question. Attach it to the verb for a general question, or to the subject/object to ask 'Is it THAT one?'.

title: Verbal Participle (Vinaiyeccam)
subtitle: Chaining sequential actions by the same subject
keyPoint: The verbal participle (வினைஎச்சம்) replaces finite verb endings to link chronological actions sharing one grammatical subject, leaving only the final verb fully conjugated.

mistakes.note: Avoid using 'மற்றும்' (and) to connect sequential verbs; Tamil uses the verbal participle (vinaiyeccam).
The verbal participle requires the same subject for all linked verbs. Use the infinitive or a conditional clause when the subject changes.
Do not leave a finite verb in the middle of a clause chain; retain the participial form until the clause concludes.

quiz.question: Chain the verbs: 'Having come home, he ate' (வா + சாப்பிட்டான்).
quiz.explanation: The verbal participle of வா (come) is வந்து, creating the sequential chain வந்து சாப்பிட்டான்.

quiz.question: Complete the sequence: 'அவள் கடிதம் ___ தபாலில் சேர்த்தாள்.' (She wrote a letter and posted it)
quiz.explanation: எழுதி is the verbal participle of எழுது (write), linking the sequential actions of writing and posting.

quiz.question: What is the verbal participle form of the strong verb பார் (see)?
quiz.explanation: Strong verbs take -த்து to form the verbal participle: பார் + த்து = பார்த்து.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly chains multiple actions?
quiz.explanation: Only the final verb takes finite tense/gender markers, while all prior verbs take participial forms (எழுந்து, கழுவி).

tip: To form the verbal participle quickly, take the past tense form of any verb and remove the final personal pronoun ending (e.g., படித்தான் minus ஆன் = படித்து).

title: Infinitive Suffix (-a) and Clause Linking
subtitle: Purposive actions, simultaneous events, and verbal complements
keyPoint: The infinitive suffix -a attaches to verbal roots to indicate purpose, trigger auxiliary verbs, or signal simultaneous background actions as an event unfolds.

mistakes.note: Do not attach the dative suffix -aaga to the infinitive to express purpose; the bare infinitive itself already denotes 'in order to'.
Auxiliary verbs like தொடங்கு (begin) must attach to the infinitive form பாட, never the bare imperative root.
Ensure correct sandhi: weak verbs take -a directly, while strong verbs take -kka.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for purpose: 'அவன் பழங்கள் ___ கடைக்குச் சென்றான்.' (to buy)
quiz.explanation: The infinitive வாங்க expresses the purpose of going to the shop ('in order to buy').

quiz.question: Choose the simultaneous clause: 'As the sun rose, the birds sang.'
quiz.explanation: The infinitive suffix on the verb denotes concurrent action (as/while the sun was rising).

quiz.question: What is the infinitive form of the strong verb கேள் (listen/ask)?
quiz.explanation: The strong verb கேள் forms its infinitive with the suffix -kka, becoming கேட்க via morphophonemic sound change.

quiz.question: Identify the infinitive in: 'நாங்கள் பாடம் கற்க பள்ளிக்குச் சென்றோம்.'
quiz.explanation: கற்க (to learn) is the infinitive form of the root கல்.

tip: Unlike the verbal participle, the infinitive can easily accommodate a change of subject between the dependent clause and the main clause.

title: Modal Auxiliaries (veendum, mudiyum, koodaadhu)
subtitle: Obligation, ability, and prohibition with dative/nominative subjects
keyPoint: Modals like வேண்டும் (must/need) and முடியும் (can) require the main verb to be in the infinitive and typically trigger a dative case subject (-ukku).

mistakes.right: எனக்கு படிக்க வேண்டும். / நான் படிக்க வேண்டும்.
mistakes.note: While colloquial Tamil often uses nominative with வேண்டும், formal Tamil strictly favors the dative case (எனக்கு) for the experiencer.

mistakes.right: அவனால் எழுத முடியும். / அவனுக்கு எழுத முடியும்.
mistakes.note: முடியும் requires either the instrumental case (-aal) or dative case (-ukku) on the agent of ability.
Remember to apply the sandhi rule: the infinitive ending in -a geminates the following stop consonant (க்) before கூடாது.

quiz.question: Complete the prohibition: 'Students must not run inside the library.' -> 'மாணவர்கள் நூலகத்தினுள் ___.'
quiz.explanation: கூடாது attached to the infinitive (ஓடக் கூடாது) expresses moral or rule-based prohibition ('must not').

quiz.question: Select the ability form: 'Can you speak English?'
quiz.explanation: Instrumental pronoun உங்களால் + infinitive பேச + modal interrogative முடியுமா forms 'Can you speak?'.

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'I must study now'?
quiz.explanation: The modal வேண்டும் preceded by the infinitive படிக்க marks absolute necessity or obligation.

quiz.question: Express refusal or non-necessity: 'You do not need to come.'
quiz.explanation: வேண்டாம் is the negative counterpart of வேண்டும், signifying 'need not' or 'do not'.

tip: Pair the modal with an infinitive for actions (படிக்க வேண்டும் = must read), or attach it directly to a noun to express desire for an object (எனக்கு காப்பி வேண்டும் = I want coffee).

title: Locative (-il, -idam) and Sociative (-oodu, -udan) Cases
subtitle: Spatial presence, personal custody, and company markers
keyPoint: Use -il for inanimate physical locations but -idam for animate beings/custody, and use -oodu/-udan to denote association and accompaniment.

mistakes.note: Never attach the inanimate locative -il to animate beings; always use -idam for persons or living entities.
The sociative suffix -udan is a bound inflectional suffix and must fuse phonologically with the base noun.
Do not attach -idam to static places or buildings; use -il for inanimate spatial locations.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'The key is with the teacher.'
quiz.explanation: The animate locative suffix -idam is mandatory when referring to something being in a person's custody or possession.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'மீன்கள் ___ வாழ்கின்றன.' (Fishes live in water)
quiz.explanation: Water is an inanimate substance, requiring the inanimate locative suffix -il (நீரில்).

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'I went with my sister'?
quiz.explanation: Accompaniment ('together with') is expressed by the sociative marker -udan / -oodu, giving தங்கையுடன்.

quiz.question: Select the correct phrase for 'Do you have money with you?'
quiz.explanation: Personal custody ('on your person') requires the animate locative suffix -idam on the second-person base, yielding உன்னிடம்.

tip: Think of -il as 'inside/at a place' and -idam as 'on one's person/in someone's possession'. Never mix them up across human and non-human boundaries!

title: Relative Participle (Peyareccam)
subtitle: Connecting verbs to nouns to form relative clauses in Tamil
keyPoint: Tamil forms relative clauses by dropping the personal ending from a tensed verb to create an adjectival participle ending in '-a' that directly precedes the noun it modifies.

cells: The action that will be done
The deed that was/is not done

mistakes.note: Do not keep the personal finite ending (-ஆன்) when qualifying a noun; use the participle form (-அ).

mistakes.wrong: வந்த மனிதன் யார் என்று எனக்குத் தெரியும் ஆனால் மனிதன் வந்தார்.
mistakes.note: Relative clauses precede the modified noun directly without standalone pronouns like English 'who' or 'which'.
Use standard literary relative participles like எழுதிய rather than colloquial spoken truncations in formal writing.

quiz.question: Which word completes: 'நேற்று காபி ___ நபர் யார்?' (The person who drank coffee yesterday)
quiz.explanation: To modify 'நபர்' with a past action, use the past relative participle 'குடித்த' (who drank).

quiz.question: Choose the present relative participle to complete: 'மேடையில் ___ பெண் அருமையாகப் பாடுகிறாள்.' (The girl who is singing on stage)
quiz.explanation: 'பாடுகிற' is the present relative participle indicating an ongoing action modifying 'பெண்'.

quiz.question: Identify the correct future relative participle in: 'அடுத்த வாரம் ___ விழா மிகச் சிறப்பானது.'
quiz.explanation: Future relative participles generally end in -உம் (-um), making 'நடக்கும்' the correct form for 'the festival that will happen'.

quiz.question: Select the negative relative participle for: 'பொய் ___ மனிதன் நல்லவன்.' (A person who does not speak lies)
quiz.explanation: The negative adjectival participle ends in -ஆத (-aadha), yielding 'சொல்லாத' (who does not speak).

tip: Tamil has no relative pronouns like 'who', 'which', or 'that'—simply turn the verb into an adjectival participle and place it immediately before the head noun.

title: Genitive Case and Postpositional Stems
subtitle: Spatial and directional relationships using oblique cases
keyPoint: Postpositions in Tamil attach to the genitive or oblique stem of nouns rather than following base nominative nouns.

mistakes.note: Nouns ending in -ai must take the genitive marker -in (-இன்) before spatial postpositions.
Nouns ending in -am form their oblique stem with -த்து- (-attu-) before taking postpositions.
The genitive suffix -உடைய (-udaiya) attaches directly to the oblique pronoun stem 'என்' to form 'என்னுடைய'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'under the tree': 'நாய் ___ படுத்திருக்கிறது.'
quiz.explanation: 'மரம்' takes the oblique inflected stem 'மரத்து' + genitive 'இன்' -> 'மரத்தின்', followed by 'கீழே'.

quiz.question: Which form correctly translates 'inside the house'?
quiz.explanation: 'வீடு' forms its oblique genitive as 'வீட்டின்' before postpositions like 'உள்ளே'.

quiz.question: Fill the blank: 'ஆசிரியர் பள்ளிக்கு ___ நிற்கிறார்.' (In front of)
quiz.explanation: 'முன்னால்' means 'in front of' and naturally pairs with dative or genitive noun stems.

quiz.question: Select the correct genitive possession: 'இது ___ புத்தகம்.' (my)
quiz.explanation: 'என்னுடைய' is the possessive/genitive form for 'my'.

tip: Neuter nouns ending in -am (like மரம் or பாடம்) always change -am to -attu (மரத்து/பாடத்து) before adding case endings or postpositions.

title: Conditional Forms (-aal) and Concessives (-aalum)
subtitle: Expressing 'if' and 'even if' structures in Tamil
keyPoint: Attach the suffix '-aal' to the past tense stem of any verb to form 'if', and add '-um' to form '-aalum' for 'even if'.

mistakes.note: While 'என்றால்' exists, the synthetic suffix '-ஆல்' directly affixed to the past stem is the standard native conditional.
Use the concessive '-ஆலும்' attached to the past verb stem to express 'even though/even if' smoothly.
Conditional is '-தால்/-ஆல்' on the past stem (பெய்தால்), not casual causal forms.

quiz.question: Complete the conditional: 'நன்றாக உழைத்___ வெற்றி பெறலாம்.' (If you work hard)
quiz.explanation: Attaching -தால் (-thaal) to the past stem 'உழைத்-' creates the conditional 'if you work hard'.

quiz.question: Which form expresses 'even if he runs'?
quiz.explanation: Adding -உம் to the conditional produces the concessive suffix '-ஆலும்' (ஓடினாலும் = even if one runs).

quiz.question: Choose the correct negative conditional: 'நீ உண்மை ___ உன்னை யாரும் நம்ப மாட்டார்கள்.' (If you don't speak)
quiz.explanation: 'பேசாவிட்டால்' combines the negative stem with 'விட்டால்' to mean 'if one does not speak'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct ending for: 'நீ அழைத்___ நான் வருவேன்.' (If you invite)
quiz.explanation: Past stem அழைத்- + ஆல் produces அழைத்தால் (if you invite).

tip: Always build the conditional from the past tense stem: செய் (root) -> செய்த்- (past stem) -> செய்தால் (if you do).

title: Aspectual Auxiliaries (vitu, kol, vai)
subtitle: Expressing completion, reflexivity, and deliberate preparation
keyPoint: Auxiliary verbs attach to the verbal participle (adverbial participle) of the main verb to indicate nuanced aspects such as total completion, self-benefit, or premeditation.

cells: I wrote it down (for later reference)

mistakes.note: Auxiliary verbs must attach to the verbal participle (சாப்பிட்டு), never directly to the bare verbal root.
The auxiliary verb carries the final subject agreement marker; it must agree with the subject in gender and number.
The auxiliary verb must follow the main verbal participle, not precede it.

quiz.question: Which auxiliary indicates that an action was finished decisively and completely?
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary verb 'விடு' (vitu) conveys conclusive, definitive completion.

quiz.question: Choose the reflexive/continuous auxiliary to complete: 'அவன் பாடம் படித்துக் ___ இருக்கிறான்.'
quiz.explanation: 'கொண்டு' (from கொள்) forms reflexive actions and continuous aspect chains like படித்துக் கொண்டிருக்கிறான்.

quiz.question: Fill the blank with the auxiliary indicating deliberate preparation for the future: 'நான் டிக்கெட் வாங்கி ___.'
quiz.explanation: 'வைத்தேன்' (from வை) expresses doing something intentionally in advance for future use.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence expressing that the bus has left completely: 'பேருந்து போய்___.'
quiz.explanation: 'விட்டது' indicates the irreversible completion of the bus having departed.

tip: Only the auxiliary verb inflects for tense, person, and number—the main verb stays locked in its adverbial participle (-i / -thu) form.

title: Participial Nouns (Vinaiyaal Anaiyum Peyar)
subtitle: Turning verbs into agent nouns meaning 'the one who does'
keyPoint: Participial nouns are created by fusing a relative participle stem with third-person pronominal endings, forming words like 'the one who came' or 'the one who does'.

cells: He who did / The man who did

mistakes.note: Using the participial noun 'வந்தவர்' is much more natural and respectful in Tamil than appending 'ஆள்'.
Participial nouns are genuine nouns and must take case suffixes when used as objects (e.g. accusative -ஐ).
Use standard relative participle roots (பாடிய-) when forming literary participial nouns.

quiz.question: Which word translates 'the woman who spoke'?
quiz.explanation: 'பேசிய' (past participle) + 'அவள்' (she) yields 'பேசியவள்' (the woman who spoke).

quiz.question: Fill the blank with the respectful form: 'இங்கே ___ என் பெரியப்பா.' (The one who came)
quiz.explanation: '-அவர்' is the polite/respectful third-person ending, giving 'வந்தவர்'.

quiz.question: Identify the future participial noun meaning 'the one who will read':
quiz.explanation: 'படிப்பவன்' is formed from the future stem and masculine ending, meaning 'he who will read'.

quiz.question: In the sentence 'ஓடியவனைப் பிடித்தார்கள்', what is the case of 'ஓடியவனை'?
quiz.explanation: The suffix '-ஐ' (ஓடியவன் + ஐ = ஓடியவனை) marks the direct object in the accusative case.

tip: Participial nouns behave entirely like standard nouns: they decline across all cases (e.g., சொன்னவர், சொன்னவரை, சொன்னவருக்கு, சொன்னவரால்).

title: Quotative Marker (enru / endru)
subtitle: Reporting speech, internal thoughts, and framing embedded clauses
keyPoint: The verbal participle என்று (enru) acts as an indispensable complementizer that closes reported speech, mental states, intentions, and named entities before the main verb.

examples.en: நாளை பள்ளிக்கு விடுமுறை என்று ஆசிரியர் கூறினார்.
அவர் நல்ல மனிதர் என்று அனைவரும் நினைக்கிறார்கள்.

mistakes.note: Unlike English, Tamil cannot place the reporting verb first; the embedded clause must precede என்று and the matrix verb.
Embedded clauses representing beliefs or thoughts require என்று before the governing cognitive verb.
Do not insert unnecessary finite copulas inside nominal complement clauses framed by என்று.

quiz.question: Complete the reported statement: 'அவன் வருவான் ___ சொன்னான்.'
quiz.explanation: என்று is the required quotative complementizer connecting the embedded statement to the verb of speaking.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly frames the thought 'It will rain'?
quiz.explanation: The thought clause precedes என்று, which immediately precedes the cognitive verb எண்ணினேன்.

quiz.question: Identify the purpose construction: 'சாப்பிடலாம் ___ கடைக்குச் சென்றான்.'
quiz.explanation: An intentional verb form followed by என்று conveys the purposive reason for going somewhere.

quiz.question: Select the correct naming clause: 'அவருக்கு முருகன் ___ பெயரிட்டார்கள்.'
quiz.explanation: Appellative naming constructions require the marker என்று preceding பெயரிடு (to name).

tip: In everyday spoken Tamil, என்று collapses into the cliticized sound 'ன்னு' (nnu), turning 'வருகிறேன் என்று' into 'வர்றேன்னு'.

title: Passive (padu) and Causative Stems
subtitle: Forming formal passives with படு and causatives with -வி/-பி and வை
keyPoint: Passives attach the auxiliary படு (padu) to the infinitive stem, while causatives employ morphological suffixes (-வி/-பி) or the periphrastic helper வை (vai).

mistakes.note: In a passive construction, the semantic agent must take the instrumental suffix -ஆல் (-aal), not the nominative case.
To express causing another person to perform an action, append the auxiliary verb வை to the infinitive.
The passive auxiliary படு must attach to the infinitive form (வெட்ட), not directly to the crude verbal root (வெட்டு).

quiz.question: How do you say 'The letter was sent by him'?
quiz.explanation: Passives take the instrumental case marker -ஆல் on the agent and the infinitive + படு construction.

quiz.question: Choose the periphrastic causative: 'The teacher made the students read.'
quiz.explanation: Infinitive படிக்க + auxiliary வைத்தார் forms the causative 'made to read'.

quiz.question: Which suffix converts the agent into the instrumental in passive sentences?
quiz.explanation: The instrumental suffix -ஆல் marks the demoted agent in Tamil passive syntax.

quiz.question: Fill the blank: 'அழுத்தமான பேச்சு அனைவரையும் சிந்திக்க ___.'
quiz.explanation: சிந்திக்க (infinitive) pairs with வைத்தது (causative of வை) to yield 'caused to think'.

tip: Passive constructions using படு are common in written journalism and formal reports, but colloquial spoken Tamil strongly prefers active voice or reflexive verbs.

title: Spoken vs Written Diglossic Shifts
subtitle: Navigating phonological erosion and verbal contraction between registers
keyPoint: Tamil exhibits strict diglossia where literary written endings systematically contract in spoken speech into nasalized vowels, retroflex mergers, and shortened aspectual markers.

useCases.label: Vowel Contraction in Aspectual Verbs
useCases.example: அவன் சாப்பிட்டுவிட்டான் என்பதற்குப் பதில் சாப்பிட்டான் என்கிறோம்.

useCases.label: Phonological Palatalization
useCases.example: செய்தான் என்பது பேச்சுத் தமிழில் செஞ்சான் என்று மாறுகிறது.

useCases.label: Colloquial Dative & Locative Shifts
useCases.example: வீட்டிற்கு என்பது பேச்சு வழக்கில் வீட்டுக்கு என்று அமைகிறது.

examples.en: எழுத்துத் தமிழில் வருகிறது என்பதைப் பேச்சுத் தமிழில் வருது என்பர்.
அவர் வந்துவிட்டார் என்பதை வந்திட்டாரு என்று சொல்வர்.
இதைச் செய்தால் நல்லது என்பதை செஞ்சா நல்லது என்பர்.
எனக்குத் தெரியாது என்பதைத் தெரில என்று சுருக்குவர்.
அங்கே போக வேண்டாம் என்பதைப் போக வேணாம் என்பர்.

mistakes.note: Spoken contracted auxiliaries like -ிட்டான் (-ittaan) should not be used in formal written Tamil essays.
Using literary endings in casual conversation sounds unnaturally stiff and archaic to native speakers.
The postposition -கிட்ட is colloquial; formal writing requires -இடம்.

quiz.question: What is the spoken colloquial equivalent of the written verb 'செய்கிறான்'?
quiz.explanation: The present marker -கிறு- weakens to -று-, turning செய்கிறான் into செய்றான் in natural spoken Tamil.

quiz.question: Which literary form corresponds to the colloquial modal 'வேணாம்' (veanaam)?
quiz.explanation: வேண்டாம் (negative optative) contracts phonologically to வேணாம் in daily spoken Tamil.

quiz.question: How does the conditional marker '-ஆல்' (e.g., வந்தால்) shift in colloquial speech?
quiz.explanation: The literary conditional suffix -ஆல் (-aal) regularly drops its lateral coda to become -ஆ (-aa), producing வந்தா.

quiz.question: Convert the literary phrase 'பார்த்துக் கொண்டிருக்கிறான்' to natural colloquial speech:
quiz.explanation: பார்த்து becomes பாத்து, and the continuous auxiliary கொண்டிருக்கிறான் collapses into -ட்டு இருக்கான்.

tip: Spoken Tamil regularly drops word-final -ம் and -ன் into nasalization of the preceding vowel, turning மரம் (maram) into 'மரா' (marõ) and அவன் (avan) into 'அவ' (avã).

title: Left-Branching Subordinate Verb Chaining
subtitle: Constructing complex periodic sentences with non-finite verbal participles
keyPoint: Tamil constructs long left-branching sentences by linking multiple adverbial participles, conditionals, and infinitives in chronological order before concluding with a single final finite verb.

useCases.label: Chronological Serial Chaining
useCases.example: காலையில் எழுந்து, குளித்து, உண்டு, பள்ளிக்குச் சென்றான்.

useCases.label: Nested Conditional Chaining
useCases.example: நேரம் கிடைத்துப் பணம் இருந்தால் சுற்றுலா போகலாம்.

examples.en: அவன் அலுவலகத்திற்குப் போய், கோப்புகளை எடுத்துக்கொண்டு, மாலையில் வீடு திரும்பினான்.
வீட்டை அடைந்து கதவைத் திறந்து விளக்கை ஏற்றினாள்.
மழை நின்று வெயில் அடித்தால் பயிர்கள் செழிக்கும்.
பணம் சேர்த்து வைத்திருந்து உரிய காலத்தில் உதவினான்.
பாடத்தைக் கவனித்துப் புரிந்து கொண்டு விடை எழுதினான்.

mistakes.note: Never coordinate actions using English-style conjunctions like 'மற்றும்'; use the verbal participle (எழுந்து) to chain clauses.
Avoid comma-splicing independent finite verbs. Subordinate the initial verb into its participial form (போய்).
Instead of inserting adverbial adverbs like பின்னர் between finite clauses, rely on the serial participle suffix chain.

quiz.question: How do you coordinate 'He cooked, ate, and slept' in genuine Tamil syntax?
quiz.explanation: Tamil chains preceding chronological actions using adverbial verbal participles (சமைத்து, உண்டு) terminating in a finite verb (தூங்கினான்).

quiz.question: Which verb form correctly fills the sequential blank: 'அவன் ஊருக்கு ___ தாயைப் பார்த்தான்'?
quiz.explanation: The verbal participle போய் links the prior clause sequentially to the final predicate.

quiz.question: What happens to tense marking in long multi-clause Tamil participial chains?
options: Every verb bears independent past tense suffixes.
Tense is marked solely on the final finite verb.
All chained verbs take future tense markers.
Tense is dropped entirely from the sentence.
quiz.explanation: Non-finite participles carry relative aspect, while tense, mood, and person are determined by the final matrix verb.

quiz.question: Select the correct combination: 'மழை ___ குடை ___ வெளியே சென்றான்.'
quiz.explanation: Both subordinate actions preceding the departure must be verbal participles: பெய்து (having rained) and எடுத்து (having taken).

tip: Only the final verb in a Tamil periodic sentence receives person-number-gender (PNG) agreements and tense inflection. All preceding actions remain non-finite.

title: Affective Discourse Clitics (-ē, -um, -tāṉ, -āvatu)
subtitle: Manipulating emphasis, exclusivity, scalar addition, and concession
keyPoint: Tamil discourse clitics attach directly to the end of any word class to modulate pragmatic stance, indicating exclusivity (-தான்), totality or addition (-உம்), emphasis (-ஏ), or minimal concession (-ஆவது).

mistakes.note: To convey exclusive focus ('he was the one who came'), attach -தான் directly to the subject pronoun.
When the universal clitic -உம் attaches to interrogative roots (e.g. எல்லாரும்), the subject is plural and requires plural agreement.
Do not duplicate restrictive particles (மட்டும்) with the minimal scalar clitic -ஆவது.

quiz.question: Which clitic expresses 'at least': 'ஒரு முறைய___ முயற்சி செய்'?
quiz.explanation: -ஆவது is the scalar minimizer clitic denoting 'at least'.

quiz.question: Choose the clitic that conveys strict exclusivity: 'அவன் ___ அதைச் செய்தான்' (He alone did it).
quiz.explanation: -தான் acts as an exclusive focus marker highlighting that specific constituent.

quiz.question: How do you emphasize 'right here' using the emphatic vowel clitic?
quiz.explanation: The clitic -ஏ appended to locatives (இங்கு + ஏ = இங்கேயே) gives the intensified meaning 'right here' / 'here itself'.

quiz.question: What is the pragmatic function of '-உம்' in 'அவனும் வந்தான்'?
quiz.explanation: -உம் serves as the additive and inclusive discourse clitic equivalent to 'also' or 'too'.

tip: When -உம் attaches to an interrogative word like யார் (who) or எங்கு (where), it converts it into a universal quantifier: யாரும் (everyone/anyone) and எங்கும் (everywhere).
